title: Caffeine three times a day, the last dose 8 hours before bed: what the sleep lab recorded [dose, recording]
teaser: Twenty young men who drink caffeine every day took 150 mg three times a day, the last dose 8 hours before bed. [sample, dose, recording] Their measured sleep did not differ from their placebo nights. [sleep_same] One thing in the brain recordings did. [sigma]
hook: The usual advice is to stop caffeine by noon. [-] A sleep laboratory tested something closer to how people actually take it: morning, midday and mid-afternoon, every day. [schedule]
populationPanel: Who was studied: twenty healthy men aged 18 to 35 who already had 300 to 600 mg of caffeine a day and slept well. [sample, who, good_sleepers] Each man went through all three conditions in random order without knowing which capsules he was taking. [blind] The result describes men like these. [lim_male] It says nothing yet about women, older adults or people who rarely have caffeine. [lim_male, lim_young, not_after_abstinence]

card.question: Does an afternoon coffee wreck your sleep? [schedule]
card.headline: Sleep showed no clear difference from placebo nights. [sleep_same]
card.support: Total sleep, time to fall asleep and sleep stages were all checked. [sleep_same]

glance.alt: Two dotted lines from waking to bed: sleep pressure keeps rising, and how tired you feel runs below it after the first dose, a gap called hidden tiredness. [schedule] Beneath, the study found no clear difference in sleep. [sleep_same]

paragraphs: All day, a tiredness signal collects in your brain. [concept:adenosine] It settles onto brain cells and slows them down, so you feel sleepy. [concept:adenosine] Caffeine takes its parking spot. [adenosine_block] The signal is still there; it just cannot land. [adenosine_block] Its name is adenosine. [adenosine_block]
Late in the day, that block can cost you sleep. [evening] Earlier studies found that evening caffeine made sleep slower to come and shorter, with less deep sleep. [evening]

A daily habit changes the picture. [tolerance] In earlier work the authors cite, a week of regular caffeine blunted its effect on sleep, even with large evening doses. [tolerance] That fits what this trial saw. [-] On caffeine, measured sleep showed no clear difference from placebo nights. [sleep_same]
The authors also suggest a daily loop. [daily_reverse] Each night, as the last dose wears off, a small withdrawal may begin. [sigma_meaning] The first dose next morning would undo it. [daily_reverse]

figure.headline: Caffeine takes the tiredness signal’s parking spot. [adenosine_block]
figure.caption: Dashed: how the authors describe caffeine acting, not measured in this study. [adenosine_block] Dotted: a sketch of the tiredness signal building up, not data. [-]
figure.alt: Two panels, each showing the surface of a brain cell with one cup-shaped dock. [-] Without caffeine, round tokens, the tiredness signal, drift down and one sits in the dock: you feel sleepy. [adenosine_block] With caffeine, a hexagon, caffeine, sits in the dock; the round tokens crowd above it and cannot land: you feel alert. [adenosine_block] How many tokens are drawn means nothing; they are a sketch, not data. [-]

paragraphs: For 10 days, the men took a capsule three times a day: 45, 255 and 475 minutes after waking. [schedule] In one condition every capsule held 150 mg of caffeine; in another, every capsule was a placebo. [dose] The third switched from caffeine to placebo after 8 days. [dose]

After 9 days, they slept in the laboratory with sensors on the scalp recording the brain. [recording] On caffeine, the night began 8 hours after the last capsule. [recording] The trial did not try a last dose closer to bed. [recording]

figure.headline: Caffeine hides tiredness. [-] It doesn’t remove it. [-]
figure.caption: Dotted: a sketch of tiredness through the day, not data. [-] The day runs from waking to bed, with the study’s three doses and the 8 hours to the sleep recording. [schedule, recording] The box is what the sleep laboratory found. [sleep_same]
figure.alt: Two dotted lines run from waking to bed. [-] One, sleep pressure, keeps rising. [-] The other, how tired you feel, follows it until the first dose, then runs below it. [schedule] The hatched gap between them is hidden tiredness, and it narrows towards bed without closing. [schedule] Nothing is drawn after bed. [-] A box beneath says what the study found: sleep showed no clear difference from placebo nights. [sleep_same]

params.title: Tiredness through a caffeine day, and what the sleep laboratory found

found.title: What this study found
found.finding: Sleep showed no clear difference from placebo nights.

audit.effect: The paper checked total sleep, time to fall asleep and the share of each sleep stage. [sleep_same] For each, it reports no clear difference between conditions, with p above 0.05. [sleep_same] It gives no size for any of these differences. [sleep_same]
audit.weakEnd: The paper gives no confidence interval for these results. [sleep_same] With twenty men, a real difference of a few minutes could hide inside “no clear difference”. [sample, lim_n] Read it as no large disruption found in this group, not proof that there is none. [sleep_same]
limitations: Only men took part, so the result may not hold for women. [lim_male]
Everyone was 18 to 35. [who] The authors say middle-aged people are more sensitive to what caffeine does to sleep. [lim_young]
Twenty men make a small trial. [sample, lim_n] Without effect sizes, nobody can say how small a difference it could have missed. [lim_n]
audit.missed: One measure did change. [-] A band of the brain’s electrical activity in sleep, called sigma, was lower on caffeine nights than on placebo nights. [sigma] The authors read it as early withdrawal, already there 8 hours after the last dose. [sigma_meaning]
more: At home, the men went to bed about 25 minutes later on caffeine than on placebo. [later_bed]
Their own ratings of how they slept showed no clear difference between conditions either. [quality_same]
The researchers expected less deep sleep on caffeine and did not find it. [no_depth_change]
The authors warn that morning caffeine could still disturb sleep after several days without any. [not_after_abstinence]

glossary.plain: A capsule that looked the same as the caffeine one but held no caffeine.

words.alt: Small round tokens drawn with dotted outlines: a sketch of the tiredness signal building up, not data. How many are drawn means nothing.

labels.signal: Tiredness signal (adenosine). It builds up while you are awake.

words.alt: Two dotted lines through a waking day: a sketch of sleep pressure building and of how tired you feel, not data. Their heights and the gap are not from the paper.

labels.narrows: The gap narrows as caffeine fades

takeaways: The schedule tested was three doses, the last one 475 minutes after waking, which came 8 hours before bed. [schedule, recording]
The finding covers a steady daily habit. [who] The authors caution that it may not hold after several days without caffeine. [not_after_abstinence]
Bedtime at home drifted about 25 minutes later on caffeine, so watch the clock as well as the cup. [later_bed]

steps.label: In bed within 30 minutes of my usual time
